extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to the Journal of Machine Learning Research (JMLR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing, submitting, and publishing manuscripts in the Journal of Machine Learning Research, including scope of acceptable content, originality rules, formatting and submission procedures, review and revision policies, and requirements for special-topic proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — new algorithms with justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish original, unpublished research reporting new algorithms with empirical, theoretical, psychological, or biological justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JMLR will publish new algorithms accompanied by appropriate justification (empirical, theoretical, psychological, or biological).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — experimental/theoretical studies yielding insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental and/or theoretical studies yielding new insight into the design and behavior of learning in intelligent systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies should provide new insight rather than merely report results; must clarify contribution to understanding design/behavior of learning systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — application accounts that shed light
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of applications of existing techniques that shed light on the strengths and weaknesses of the methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application papers should illuminate method properties (strengths/weaknesses), not just describe an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — formalization of new learning tasks and assessment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Formalization of new learning tasks (e.g., in the context of new applications) and of methods for assessing performance on those tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers that define new tasks or evaluation methodologies should include clearly defined assessment methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — development of analytical frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of new analytical frameworks that advance theoretical studies of practical learning methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks should advance theoretical understanding of practical methods and be well-motivated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — computational models of natural learning systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Computational models of data from natural learning systems at the behavioral or neural level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should be computational and pertain to behavioral or neural data, with appropriate justification and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — well-written surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Extremely well-written surveys of existing work will also be considered for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys must be exceptionally well written; not all surveys will be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript quality — concise, complete, and polished
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be concise and complete; manuscripts should be carefully proofread and polished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that do not meet these criteria may be returned unreviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for claims
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims should be clearly articulated and supported either by empirical experiments or theoretical analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide evidence/analysis backing claims; unsupported claims are inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation and demonstration encouraged; reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, authors are encouraged to implement their work and to demonstrate its utility on significant problems; any experiments reported should be reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to include implementations, demonstrations, and reproducible experimental details (datasets, code, instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems papers — describe contributions/principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers describing systems should clearly describe the contributions or the principles underlying the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System descriptions must state the underlying principles and clearly delineate contributions rather than merely describing implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical results — discuss practical utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers describing theoretical results should also discuss their practical utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theoretical work should include discussion of applicability or implications for practice where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-of-the-art advancement and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be clear how the work advances the current state of understanding and why the advance matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers must situate contributions relative to prior work and explain the significance of the advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should report on what was learned in doing the work, rather than merely on what was done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize insights and interpretation, not just procedures or engineering steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge predecessors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must clearly acknowledge the contributions of their predecessors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and discuss relevant prior work and give credit where due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce new terminology/techniques only with justification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper introduces new terminology or techniques, it should also explain why current terminology or techniques are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must motivate the need for new terms or methods and relate them to existing concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality — prior and concurrent publication rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted work cannot have been published previously or be pending publication in another journal. Research published or under consideration at workshops or conferences is considered only if the JMLR submission goes into greater depth and extends the published results in a substantive way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must notify JMLR about previous or pending conference publication at the time of submission; conference/workshop versions are acceptable only with substantive extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and accepted file types
rubrics_metrics.description: JMLR accepts submissions via its electronic submission management system; articles must be submitted in electronic form; either PostScript or PDF is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be sent through http://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/manudb and may be in PostScript or PDF (Word allowed earlier in Prepare steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting — layout and font
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be in single column format, typeset in 11 point font or larger, and should include all author contact information on the first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not required, JMLR format is encouraged (see authors guide). Use the provided style files/templates when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online appendices and source code policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles may be accompanied by online appendices containing data, demonstrations, instructions for obtaining source code, or the source code itself if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JMLR strongly encourages authors to include such appendices. Note: if an online appendix contains source code, a software release form releasing JMLR from liability must be signed prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: File preparation and size constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare submissions in PDF, PostScript, or Microsoft Word format; if multiple files create an archive (tar or zip). Ensure the file to be uploaded is less than 5Mb in size and that the file extension indicates the type (.ps or .pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these steps before upload to avoid technical problems; rename files appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title page must contain complete name, postal and e-mail address of the corresponding author; a condensed running title of fifty (50) characters or less; a list of five key-words; and an abstract that does not exceed 200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include required title page information may delay processing; adhere to the character/word limits provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review decisions and revision policy
rubrics_metrics.description: JMLR reviewers make recommendations to accept or reject. If a paper requires substantial revisions, it will not be accepted; the editor may recommend that the author submit a revised version, but there is no guarantee it will be reviewed by the same referees or that it will eventually be published. A paper may be revised and resubmitted at most once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid misunderstandings, authors are encouraged to contact the editor prior to resubmission with any salient questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor revisions and revision timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is accepted, the editor and reviewers may require minor revisions. Normally, authors will have up to three months to accomplish their revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receiving a revised paper the editor may, at their discretion, ask the reviewers to re-review the revised paper. Electronic publication occurs immediately upon receipt of the final version of an accepted article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and publication materials
rubrics_metrics.description: When a paper is accepted, authors retain ownership of the copyright, but must sign a copyright agreement form giving MIT Press the right to publish the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to provide HTML versions of the paper and electronic forms of any applicable data sets or executable code; HTML versions should be identical in content to the PS/PDF article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged post-acceptance actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to add links to the article and the JMLR site on their personal web pages and may create pages pointing to subsequent related research; JMLR will maintain a link from the original paper to this page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may contact the executive editor to publish forward pointers to related subsequent articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special topics — rationale and operation
rubrics_metrics.description: JMLR will accept proposals for special topics (instead of special issues); special topics operate similarly but papers will not appear contiguously in print and will be published individually as ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special topics are collected incrementally on a special web page rather than waiting for all final versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposing a special topic — required proposal elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should outline: topic area and why it is important; guest editors' expertise in the technical area and with reviewing/editing; plan for circulating the call for papers; dates for submission, accept/reject decisions, and final versions; desired number of pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action editors will discuss and make accept/reject decisions on proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats for special topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Special topics tend to have somewhat lower quality papers than regular issues; special topics almost always run late; guest editors almost always underestimate the amount of work required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of these risks and plan to keep quality and schedule in check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting resources and common errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are provided with an authors guide, reviewer guide, formatting instructions, common formatting errors list, annotated sample paper sources, LaTeX style, LyX layout files, and a Microsoft Word template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided resources (style files, templates, sample paper) and consult the common formatting errors page to avoid submission problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to publish and software release forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must complete a permission to publish form and, if executable code is made available as part of an online appendix, a software release form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms are available in multiple formats (Word/PS/PDF) and must be sent to the MIT Press contact as instructed.
